item.title: Open call: 2026 FRAME Mentoring programme
item.description: Applications are now open for the 2026 edition of the FRAME Mentoring programme for junior professionals in the audio-visual heritage sector. The deadline for submissions is 22 March 2026. The initiative forms part of the wider FRAME training programme, organised by INA for more than 15 years in partnership with FIAT/IFTA and EBU Academy. item.title: Spotify and Sony to mark 10 years of Kwesta’s DaKAR II
item.description: Spotify and Sony Music Entertainment will host a live event in Randburg, Johannesburg, to mark a decade since the release of Kwesta’s double album DaKAR II. The celebration will honour the project’s impact on South African hip hop since its release in 2016. At the time of its debut, DaKAR II was noted for its ambitious scale and distinctly South African storytelling. Ten years on, the album continues to attract significant streaming activity. item.title: Open call: IDFA Bertha Fund
item.description: The IDFA Bertha Fund (IBF) is accepting entries for its IBF Europe – Minority Co-Production funding scheme. The deadline for submissions is 1 April 2026. The scheme aims to support European producers participating as minority co-producers in feature-length documentary projects led by filmmakers from Africa, Asia, Eastern Europe, Latin America, the Caribbean and Oceania. item.title: Open call: 2026 Artist-in-Residence Programme in Durban
item.description: The BAT Centre in Durban has issued an open call for its 2026 Artist-in-Residence (AIR) Programme. The 12-month, full-time residency is aimed at visual artists and musicians aged between 18 and 25. The programme is designed to support emerging creatives through structured development and access to professional facilities. item.title: Suno reports two million paid subscribers, $300m in annual revenue
item.description: AI music generator Suno has reached two million paid subscribers and $300 million in annual recurring revenue (ARR), according to its chief executive and co-founder Mikey Shulman. Shulman disclosed the figures in a LinkedIn post on 25 February, two years after the platform’s launch. item.title: SA: Gallo Music marks 100 years with centenary celebrations
item.description: Gallo Music, South Africa’s oldest record label, is set to celebrate its 100th anniversary, cementing its legacy as a defining force in both national and global music. The milestone highlights a century of discovering, nurturing, and promoting influential artists and genres across the continent. item.title: Metro FM Music Awards 2026: Sam Deep leads the nominations
item.description: South African amapiano producer and DJ Sam Deep has emerged as the most nominated artist at the 2026 Metro FM Music Awards, securing nods across several major categories. The nominees were announced at The Forum in Hyde Park, in Johannesburg, on 26 February ahead of the awards ceremony at the Durban ICC on 25 April. item.title: SA: Funky Qla concludes Dark or Durban series with New EP
item.description: By Abraham Rampai South African musician Funky Qla has released Dark or Durban 3: The Last Chapter, a six-track EP marking the final instalment of his Dark or Durban series and setting the stage for his debut album in 2026. The project underscores his reputation as a compelling storyteller in the local music scene. The EP opens with ‘Isono’, featuring Zeh McGeba, which presents a raw exploration of love and heartbreak. item.title: The Brother Moves On: A Fearless Fusion of Afrocentric sound, political reflection
item.description: In today’s turbulent global political landscape, The Brother Moves On acts as a voice for those impacted by systemic failures. Their 2022 album, $/He Who Feeds You Owns You, is a provocative work that sparks conversation both in its production and its themes. item.title: Sarkodie, WAVVI grant 250 Ghanaian artists free Royal Albert Hall livestream
item.description: West African music distribution platform WAVVI has partnered with award-winning Ghanaian rapper Sarkodie to provide 250 independent Ghanaian artists with free access to the livestream of his sold-out Rapperholic concert at London’s Royal Albert Hall on 6 March. The initiative coincides with Ghana Independence Day and aims to support emerging artists by granting them a front-row digital view of a major international performance.
